why.heading: How patients find a doctor
why.body: The patient journey usually starts with a condition or symptom search, moves to comparing specialists, and ends with practical checks: location, availability, insurance, reviews. Google holds health content to its highest standard, favoring content with clear expertise behind it. Your profiles matter enormously: Healthgrades, Zocdoc, Google, patients cross-check everywhere. The practices that win make every one of those touchpoints consistent, credible, and easy to act on.

section1.heading: Condition and treatment pages that rank
section1.body: I build dedicated pages for the conditions you treat and the procedures you perform, written in language patients understand and structured around their real questions. Every medical claim is drafted for your review, because accuracy is non-negotiable and you sign off on all of it. Doctor bio pages get proper depth: credentials, special interests, philosophy of care, because patients choose people. This content earns rankings because it genuinely serves the searcher, which is exactly what Google wants for health queries.

section2.heading: Profiles, reviews, and local trust
section2.body: Your Google Business Profile, health directories, and review footprint get rebuilt consistently: correct specialties, services, hours, insurance information, and real photos of your practice. Patient reviews are handled carefully and within healthcare rules: I set up compliant ways to encourage feedback and respond professionally. Local SEO ties it together so 'near me' searches for your specialty surface your practice first. The goal is simple: when a patient compares you against two alternatives, you are the obvious choice.

faqs.q: Is medical SEO different from regular SEO?
faqs.a: The foundations are the same, but health content faces stricter quality evaluation and every medical claim has to be accurate and expert-approved. The bar is higher, so the process is more careful. That is the whole difference.
I draft it from reputable sources and your input, then you or your clinical lead approves every word before publication. Nothing medical goes live without a qualified sign-off.

faqs.q: Can you help us get more patient reviews?
faqs.a: Yes, using compliant methods only. I set up ethical review flows and response templates that respect healthcare regulations: no incentives, no cherry-picking, and no responses that reveal anything about a patient's care.

faqs.q: How long before SEO brings new patients?
faqs.a: Typically four to eight months for competitive specialties, with local and profile work often moving sooner. Medical SEO is slow by design, because trust is built carefully, not manufactured.

faqs.q: Do you work with single-doctor practices?
faqs.a: Yes. Smaller practices often have an advantage: a real doctor's voice and genuine expertise beat corporate clinic copy every time.

faqs.q: Will you promise a number of new patients?
faqs.a: No. I will not promise patient volumes or specific ranking positions to anyone, in any industry. What you get is honest work, clear reporting, and content your peers would respect.
